verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's own docs describe targeting conditions on SDK-passed attributes such as user IDs and emails, saved groups, and layered rules that force a value for beta testers above a general rollout. That covers including specific individual users. Explicit exclusion or deny-list semantics are not shown, and nothing describes per-user allowlist management in depth. missing for 10: explicit documentation of excluding specific users (deny-lists), detail on saved-group/ID-list allowlist handling, independent or hands-on corroboration of individual-user targeting.

support.subject: As a developer, I can target or exclude specific individual users for a flag (allowlists, beta testers, internal accounts)

citations.quote: Layer multiple rules on one feature to compose behavior — for example, a forced value for beta testers above a gradual rollout to everyone else.
Target feature flags with user attributes, conditions, saved groups, and percentage rollouts.
The actual values of targeting attributes (e.g., user IDs, emails) are never sent to GrowthBook.
Add targeting conditions to a rule to control which values a user sees. Conditions are evaluated against attributes you pass into the SDK
